root_cause.text: The pipapo_drop() function unconditionally accesses rulemap[i + 1].n as a function argument on every loop iteration, including the final iteration where i == m->field_count - 1, causing an out-of-bounds read of the stack-allocated rulemap array which has size NFT_PIPAPO_MAX_FIELDS (16 elements).
root_cause.evidence: The patch demonstrates that rulemap[i + 1].n is read at the call site before pipapo_unmap() executes, even though the function only uses to_offset when is_last is false. The KASAN report confirms the read occurs at offset 164, exactly 4 bytes past the end of the rulemap array (which occupies offsets 32-160). The fix adds a bounds check (last = i == m->field_count - 1) and conditionally passes 0 instead of rulemap[i + 1].n on the last iteration, preventing the out-of-bounds access.

intent_record.intent_summary: Extract the last-field detection logic into a reusable boolean variable to enable conditional field-specific processing within the loop.
intent_record.what: Added a new local variable `bool last` that is assigned the result of comparing the loop index `i` against `m->field_count - 1` at the beginning of the nft_pipapo_for_each_field loop body.
intent_record.how: This change introduces a boolean flag that identifies whether the current iteration is processing the last field in the pipapo match structure. This flag can be used in subsequent code within the loop to conditionally execute logic specific to the final field iteration, enabling field-specific handling without recalculating the comparison multiple times.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix potential out-of-bounds array access by passing 0 instead of rulemap[i + 1].n when processing the last field in pipapo_drop().
intent_record.what: Changed the fourth and fifth arguments passed to pipapo_unmap() from 'rulemap[i + 1].n, i == m->field_count - 1' to 'last ? 0 : rulemap[i + 1].n, last', where 'last' is a boolean variable indicating whether the current field is the last one.
intent_record.how: This change modifies the logic for determining what value to pass as the fourth argument to pipapo_unmap(). Instead of always passing rulemap[i + 1].n and separately indicating if this is the last field, it now conditionally passes 0 when 'last' is true, or rulemap[i + 1].n when false. The fifth argument is simplified from a computed boolean expression to the direct 'last' variable. This prevents out-of-bounds access to rulemap[i + 1] when processing the final field, since rulemap[i + 1] would be invalid when i is at the last index.

bic_trace_step.reason: The pipapo_drop() function at lines 1854-1880 contains the vulnerable construct. The function iterates through fields using 'nft_pipapo_for_each_field(f, i, m)' where i goes from 0 to m->field_count-1. On line 1877, the code unconditionally accesses 'rulemap[i + 1].n' as an argument to pipapo_unmap(): 'pipapo_unmap(f->mt, f->rules, rulemap[i].to, rulemap[i].n, rulemap[i + 1].n, i == m->field_count - 1)'. When i == m->field_count - 1 (the final iteration), this accesses rulemap[m->field_count], which is out-of-bounds for the stack-allocated rulemap array of size NFT_PIPAPO_MAX_FIELDS (16 elements). The rulemap array is declared at line 1854 as 'union nft_pipapo_map_bucket rulemap[]' with no bounds checking before accessing rulemap[i+1] in the loop. The fix would require checking if this is the last field before accessing rulemap[i+1], but no such check exists in this code.
